title: The Cuban Missile Crisis, 1962 — thirteen days, and the officer who said no
sources: Wikipedia: Cuban Missile Crisis — a 13-day confrontation (16–28 October 1962), widely considered the closest the Cold War came to full-scale nuclear war; on 14 October a U-2 flown by Major Richard Heyser took 928 pictures over Cuba; on 15 October analysts identified objects that appeared to be medium-range ballistic missiles; the next morning (16 October) Bundy showed Kennedy the U-2 photographs; the Joint Chiefs unanimously agreed a full-scale attack and invasion was the only solution; Kennedy chose a naval blockade, called a 'quarantine'; on 27 October Major Rudolf Anderson's U-2 was shot down over Cuba; on 28 October Khrushchev announced the dismantling of the weapons; the US secretly agreed to remove its Jupiter missiles from Turkey (and Italy)
Wikipedia: Richard S. Heyser — his U-2 photographs revealed Soviet medium-range ballistic missiles in Cuba, 14 October 1962

Wikipedia: Vasily Arkhipov — on 27 October 1962 US destroyers detected submarine B-59 near Cuba and dropped practice depth charges; its captain and political officer believed war had begun and prepared to launch a nuclear torpedo; Arkhipov, the executive officer, refused, and his decision prevented the use of nuclear weapons
Wikipedia: Rudolf Anderson — killed when his U-2 was shot down over Cuba

post.facebook:
On this day in 1962, President Kennedy was shown the photographs that began the Cuban Missile Crisis — the closest the Cold War came to full-scale nuclear war.

Two days earlier, U-2 pilot Major Richard Heyser had taken 928 pictures over Cuba. Analysts found Soviet medium-range ballistic missile sites. Kennedy's Joint Chiefs wanted an attack and an invasion; he chose a naval blockade instead, and called it a "quarantine".

On 27 October, the most dangerous day, Major Rudolf Anderson's U-2 was shot down over Cuba, and he was killed. The same day, US destroyers dropped practice depth charges on the Soviet submarine B-59. Its captain believed war had begun and prepared a nuclear torpedo. The executive officer, Vasily Arkhipov, refused — and his decision prevented the use of nuclear weapons.

The next day Khrushchev agreed to remove the missiles. In secret, the United States agreed to remove its own Jupiter missiles from Turkey.

Also on 16 October: fire destroyed most of the Palace of Westminster (1834), and Walt and Roy Disney founded their cartoon studio (1923).

youtube.description:
16 October 1962: President Kennedy is shown U-2 photographs of Soviet nuclear missile sites in Cuba, taken two days earlier by Major Richard Heyser. His military chiefs want an invasion; he chooses a naval "quarantine". Thirteen days follow — the closest the Cold War came to nuclear war. On 27 October a U-2 is shot down, and a Soviet submarine under practice depth charges prepares a nuclear torpedo — until its executive officer, Vasily Arkhipov, refuses. Khrushchev withdraws the missiles; in secret, the US removes its own from Turkey.

Also on 16 October: the burning of the Palace of Westminster (1834) and the founding of the Disney Brothers Cartoon Studio (1923).
